_help: Track A: Citation formats. Items are grouped by stage. See README.md, section 'How to add or edit an item'.
title: Citation formats

sourceCards.title: Why students skip breakfast
sourceCards.idea: Many first-year students skip breakfast because their classes start early.

items.prompt: You want to cite this source in brackets at the end of your sentence. Which citation is correct?
items.rule: Parenthetical: (Surname, year), with a comma before the year. Use the surname only, no initials.
items.hint: Look at what comes between the name and the year.

sourceCards.title: Green roofs in hot cities
sourceCards.idea: Plants on roofs can keep buildings cooler in summer.

items.prompt: You want to cite this source in brackets at the end of your sentence. Which citation is correct?
items.rule: Two authors inside brackets: join the names with &, e.g. (Lee & Okafor, 2020).
items.hint: Inside brackets, one small symbol joins the two names.

sourceCards.title: Part-time work and study
sourceCards.idea: Students who work long hours have less time for reading.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Mensah and Petrova (2020) found that long working hours leave students less time for reading.
Mensah & Petrova (2020) found that long working hours leave students less time for reading.
Mensah and Petrova, (2020) found that long working hours leave students less time for reading.
acceptedAnswers: Mensah and Petrova (2020) found that long working hours leave students less time for reading.
items.rule: Two authors in the sentence: join the names with “and”, e.g. Lee and Okafor (2020).
items.hint: The names are part of the sentence here, not inside brackets.

sourceCards.title: Group work online
sourceCards.idea: Online group work is easier when each member has a clear role.

items.prompt: You want to cite this source in brackets at the end of your sentence. Which citation is correct?
items.rule: Three or more authors: first author + et al. from the first citation. Full stop after “al” only.
items.hint: There are three authors. How many names do you need?

sourceCards.title: Learning in a second language
sourceCards.quote: Confidence grows when students are allowed to make mistakes.

items.prompt: You quote these exact words from the source. Which citation is correct?
items.rule: A direct quotation needs a page: (Author, year, p. 15). Use pp. for a range and para. if there are no pages.
items.hint: A quotation needs the page. Think about the order and the small abbreviation.

sourceCards.title: Cycling to campus
sourceCards.idea: Safe bike lanes encourage students to cycle.

sourceCards.title: How students travel
sourceCards.idea: Students cycle more when bike lanes are protected.

items.prompt: You cite both sources in one bracket. Which citation is correct?
items.rule: Several works in one bracket: alphabetical order by surname, separated by semicolons.
items.hint: Think about the order of the names, and the mark between the two works.

sourceCards.title: Tips for group presentations
sourceCards.idea: Practise your presentation together at least once before the day.

items.prompt: You want to cite this source in brackets at the end of your sentence. Which citation is correct?
items.rule: No date: write n.d. in place of the year, with two full stops.
items.hint: The web page has no date. APA uses a short abbreviation.

sourceCards.title: Bus use in growing cities
sourceCards.idea: Bus use rises when buses come more often.

items.prompt: This is the FIRST time you cite this source in your essay. Which citation is correct?
items.rule: Group author, first citation: full name + abbreviation in square brackets, e.g. (National Centre for Urban Transport [NCUT], 2021).
items.hint: The first time, readers need the full name and the short form. Look at the type of brackets.

sourceCards.title: Bus use in growing cities
sourceCards.idea: Bus use rises when buses come more often.

items.prompt: You have ALREADY cited this source once, with its abbreviation. Which citation is correct now?
items.rule: Group author after the first citation: use only the abbreviation, e.g. (NCUT, 2021).
items.hint: After the first time, use the short form only.

sourceCards.title: Commuting and wellbeing
sourceCards.idea: Long commutes are linked to lower wellbeing among students.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Tanaka et al. (2023) reported that long commutes are linked to lower student wellbeing.
Tanaka et al (2023) reported that long commutes are linked to lower student wellbeing.
Tanaka, et al. (2023) reported that long commutes are linked to lower student wellbeing.
acceptedAnswers: Tanaka et al. (2023) reported that long commutes are linked to lower student wellbeing.
items.rule: Three or more authors: first author + et al. from the first citation. Full stop after “al” only.
items.hint: Check the full stop and the comma.

sourceCards.title: Reading beyond the classroom
sourceCards.quote: Reading for pleasure is not a luxury that schools can add when exams are over. It builds the vocabulary, patience and curiosity that every subject depends on, and students who read widely outside class often find academic texts less frightening than those who do not.

items.prompt: This quotation is 45 words long. How should it appear in your essay?
options: As an indented block with no quotation marks. The citation comes after the final full stop.
In the normal paragraph, inside quotation marks, with the citation before the final full stop.
As an indented block inside quotation marks, with the citation before the final full stop.
acceptedAnswers: As an indented block with no quotation marks. The citation comes after the final full stop.
items.rule: 40 words or more: block quotation, no quotation marks, citation after the final full stop.
items.hint: Long quotations look different on the page. Think about quotation marks and where the citation goes.

items.prompt: When does a quotation need the block format?
options: When it is 40 words or more
When it is 20 words or more
When it is longer than one line
acceptedAnswers: When it is 40 words or more
items.rule: 40 words or more: block quotation, no quotation marks, citation after the final full stop.
items.hint: Count the words in the quotation.

items.rule: Parenthetical: (Surname, year), with a comma before the year. Use the surname only, no initials. A page number for a paraphrase depends on your course: see the note after you answer.
items.hint: This is a paraphrase, not a quotation. Is the page needed? Your course setting decides.

sourceCards.title: How students read
sourceCards.idea: First-year students read more on phones than on laptops.

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.
items.frame: ___ found that first-year students read more on their phones than on laptops.
items.rule: Narrative: the author's name is part of the sentence and only the year goes in brackets: Lee (2020).
items.hint: The gap is the subject of the verb “found”.

sourceCards.title: Short study sessions
sourceCards.idea: Short study sessions help students remember more.

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.
items.frame: Students who study in short, regular sessions tend to remember more of what they learn ___.
items.rule: Parenthetical: author and year both go in brackets, usually at the end of the idea: (Lee, 2020).
items.hint: The sentence is already complete. The citation just adds the source.

sourceCards.title: Safer roads near schools
sourceCards.idea: Cycling lanes reduce accidents near schools.

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.
items.frame: According to ___, cycling lanes reduce traffic accidents near schools.
items.rule: Two authors in the sentence: join the names with “and”, e.g. Lee and Okafor (2020).
items.hint: “According to” is followed by the names. Brackets only around the year.

sourceCards.title: Cooler buildings
sourceCards.idea: Rooftop gardens lower building temperatures in summer.

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.
items.frame: Rooftop gardens can lower the temperature inside city buildings during the hottest summer months ___.
items.rule: Two authors inside brackets: join the names with &, e.g. (Lee & Okafor, 2020).
items.hint: The idea comes first, so the whole citation goes in brackets. & or “and”?

sourceCards.title: Bilingual children and attention
sourceCards.idea: Bilingual children may switch between tasks more easily.

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.
items.frame: ___ {suggest|suggested} that bilingual children may switch between tasks more easily.
items.rule: Three or more authors: first author + et al. from the first citation. Full stop after “al” only.
items.hint: The gap is the subject. There are three authors.

sourceCards.idea: Classroom noise makes it harder to concentrate.

sourceCards.title: Quiet classrooms

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.
items.frame: Several studies have linked classroom noise to poor concentration ___.
items.rule: Several works in one bracket: alphabetical order by surname, separated by semicolons.
items.hint: Two sources, one bracket. Think about order and the mark between them.

sourceCards.title: Public transport and price

items.rule: Narrative: the author's name is part of the sentence and only the year goes in brackets: Lee (2020).
items.hint: “As … notes” needs a name in the sentence.

items.rule: Narrative: the author's name is part of the sentence and only the year goes in brackets: Lee (2020). The page goes in brackets after the quotation.

sourceCards.title: Homework and families
sourceCards.quote: a bridge between school and home

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.

items.rule: A direct quotation needs a page: (Author, year, p. 15). Use pp. for a range and para. if there are no pages.
items.hint: Idea first, so everything goes in brackets: author, year and page.

sourceCards.title: Exam weeks and sleep

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.

items.rule: Two authors in the sentence: join the names with “and”, e.g. Lee and Okafor (2020).
items.hint: “A study by” is followed by the names in the sentence.

sourceCards.title: Working from home: a review
sourceCards.idea: Working from home suits some jobs better than others.

items.prompt: Does this gap need a narrative citation (name in the sentence) or a parenthetical one (everything in brackets)? Build it.
items.frame: In a recent review, ___ {argue|argued} that working from home suits some jobs better than others.
items.rule: Three or more authors: first author + et al. from the first citation. Full stop after “al” only.
items.hint: The gap is the subject of the verb. Three authors.
